mainTopic: Returning a found שטר חוב without אחריות נכסים: רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן explain the משנה's מחלוקת, and a ברייתא refutes רבי אלעזר.
overview: The amud first finishes an earlier line about a borrower who says the loan never happened. Then two אמוראים explain the משנה's argument between רבי מאיר and the רבנן about returning a found loan document that has no property guarantee. רבי אלעזר says they argue when the borrower denies the debt. רבי יוחנן says they argue when the borrower admits it. Each one also explains how much such a document can collect in each opinion. The גמרא then quotes a ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן. It shows that, for רבי מאיר, a note without a guarantee still collects from free property. It also shows that everyone worries about קנוניא, since a guaranteed note is not returned even when both sides agree. Finally, the גמרא asks why this counts as only one refutation of רבי אלעזר when two of his claims were disproved.

steps.title: Finishing the earlier point: the borrower says the loan never happened
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of an earlier line describe the borrower as someone who claims the loan never took place.
steps.simpleTranslation: …the one who says, 'These things never happened.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence from the earlier discussion. It describes the borrower as a person who says there never was a loan at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A borrower who says the loan never happened is calling the document fake. So he cannot claim the paper as his own. This wraps up the earlier explanation before a new topic begins.

keyTerms.meaning: 'These things never happened': a total denial that the loan ever took place

phrases.english: who says: these things never happened.
phrases.notes: This is the end of a sentence from just before. He means the borrower is saying there was never any loan, so the note must be fake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the line of discussion from before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The borrower has no claim to the paper, because he says the loan never happened.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: they argue when the borrower denies the debt
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the משנה's argument is about a borrower who denies the debt. It depends on how much a note without a property guarantee can collect. If the borrower admits, everyone agrees to return the note.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The argument is when the borrower does not admit. רבי מאיר holds that a note with no property guarantee collects nothing, neither from sold property nor from free property. The רבנן hold that it cannot collect from sold property, but it does collect from free property. But when the borrower admits, everyone agrees the note is returned. We do not worry that it was already paid, and we do not worry about a plot between the lender and borrower.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר explains the case where רבי מאיר and the רבנן argue: the borrower denies owing the money. He also explains the reasoning behind each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, a note like this collects nothing at all, so returning it cannot hurt a borrower who may have already paid. For the רבנן, it still collects from the borrower's free property, so returning it is risky. When the borrower admits the debt, there is no fear of earlier payment or of a plot, so all agree to return it.

keyTerms.meaning: The borrower admits he owes the money
A property guarantee: a clause tying the borrower's land to the loan
Liened property that was already sold to buyers
Free property still owned by the borrower
Repayment: the worry that the loan was already paid
A plot between lender and borrower to cheat others

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of land. 'מְשַׁעְבְּדֵי' is land the borrower already sold to someone else. 'בְּנֵי חָרֵי' is land he still owns. The whole argument depends on which of these the note can collect from.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
The dispute is when the liable party does not admit.
phrases.notes: The 'dispute' is the argument in the משנה between רבי מאיר and the רבנן about returning a found note.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Meir holds:
a note that has no property guarantee
does not collect, neither from liened (sold) property
nor from free property.
And the Rabbis hold:
it is only from liened property that it does not collect,
but from free property, it certainly collects.
But when the liable party admits,
everyone agrees he must return it,
and we are not concerned about repayment or collusion.
phrases.notes: The 'collusion' worry is that the lender and borrower might team up to use an old note to take land from people who bought from the borrower.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּשֶׁאֵין חַיָּיב מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how to explain the משנה's argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is when the borrower denies the debt. רבי מאיר holds the note collects nothing. The רבנן hold it collects from free property. When the borrower admits, all agree the note is returned.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: they argue when the borrower admits the debt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reverses רבי אלעזר. The argument is when the borrower admits, and it is about collecting from sold property. When the borrower denies, everyone agrees not to return the note.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The argument is when the borrower admits. רבי מאיר holds that a note with no property guarantee cannot collect from sold property, but it does collect from free property. The רבנן hold it collects from sold property too. But when the borrower does not admit, everyone agrees the note is not returned, because we worry it was already paid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different explanation of the משנה. He says the argument is in the case where the borrower admits the debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, this note cannot reach sold land, so returning it cannot hurt buyers through a plot. For the רבנן, it can reach sold land, so there is a risk of a plot against buyers. When the borrower denies the debt, both sides fear it was already paid, so no one returns it.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too
We are concerned about

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: they argue when the borrower denies, and if he admits, everyone returns the note. רבי יוחנן: they argue when the borrower admits, and if he denies, no one returns it. In each reading, the רבנן give a note without אחריות נכסים one more level of strength than רבי מאיר does. For רבי אלעזר it is nothing versus free property. For רבי יוחנן it is free property versus sold property too.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The dispute is when the liable party admits,
for Rabbi Meir holds:
a note that has no property guarantee
it is only from liened property that it does not collect,
but from free property, it certainly collects.
And the Rabbis hold:
it collects from liened property too.
But when the liable party does not admit,
everyone agrees he should not return it,
because we are concerned about repayment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מַחְלוֹקֶת כְּשֶׁחַיָּיב מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite explanation from רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is when the borrower admits. רבי מאיר holds the note collects only from free property. The רבנן hold it collects from sold property too. When the borrower denies, all agree not to return the note.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן and disproves רבי אלעזר and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces a ברייתא that agrees with רבי יוחנן. It disproves one point of רבי אלעזר and two points of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רבי יוחנן. It disproves רבי אלעזר on one point and disproves שמואל on two points.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It announces that a ברייתא backs רבי יוחנן, and the ברייתא itself will be quoted next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same source both supports one view and knocks down others. The גמרא counts the refutation of רבי אלעזר as one point and the refutation of שמואל as two. The details will become clear once the ברייתא is quoted, and Step 9 questions why רבי אלעזר's refutation counts as only one.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him
A refutation: a source that disproves an אמורא's view
On one point
On two points

phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan,
and it is a refutation of Rabbi Elazar on one point,
and a refutation of Shmuel on two points.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to decide between the explanations in steps 2 and 3.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's explanation of the משנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא, which will be quoted next

steps.title: The ברייתא's rulings on found loan documents
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that a found note with אחריות נכסים is never returned, even if both sides agree. A note without it is returned only if the borrower admits. This is the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone found loan documents that include a property guarantee, he should not return them to either side, even if both agree. If they have no property guarantee, he returns it to the lender when the borrower admits. If the borrower does not admit, he returns it to neither side. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the text of the ברייתא it promised in Step 4. This is the source that will be used against רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא splits found notes into two kinds: with אחריות נכסים and without. With it, agreement between both sides is not enough to return the note. Without it, the borrower's admission is enough to return it to the lender.

keyTerms.meaning: Loan documents (promissory notes)
A property guarantee: a clause tying the borrower's land to the debt
Borrower / lender
He should not return it

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the surprise: with a property guarantee, the note is NOT returned even when both borrower and lender agree. Agreement does not solve everything here.

phrases.english: If he found loan documents
and they include a property guarantee,
even though both of them agree,
phrases.notes: "Both" means the lender and the borrower both agree the loan is real and still unpaid.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַחְזִיר לֹא לָזֶה וְלֹא לָזֶה.
phrases.english: he should not return it, not to this one and not to that one.
If they do not include a property guarantee,
when the borrower admits, he should return it to the lender;
if the borrower does not admit,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַחְזִיר לֹא לָזֶה וְלֹא לָזֶה,
phrases.english: he should not return it, not to this one and not to that one.
These are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָצָא שִׁטְרֵי חוֹב וְיֵשׁ בָּהֶם אַחְרָיוּת נְכָסִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the actual text of the ברייתא announced in Step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's reading, against רבי אלעזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the view of רבי מאיר

steps.title: רבי מאיר's reason and the view of the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains: for רבי מאיר, a note with אחריות נכסים collects from sold land, while one without it collects only from unsold land. The חכמים say both kinds collect from sold land.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי מאיר used to say: a note that includes a property guarantee collects from sold property, and one that does not include a property guarantee collects from free property. The חכמים say: both kinds collect from sold property.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and gives the reason behind רבי מאיר's rulings. It also adds the opposing view of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger with a found note is that it can be used to take land from buyers. So a note that can reach sold land is never returned, while a note that can only reach the borrower's own land is returned if he admits. For the חכמים every note reaches sold land, so they would not return either kind.

keyTerms.meaning: Collects (the debt)
Property the borrower already sold to others but which is still tied to the debt
"Free" property the borrower still owns
The Sages, the majority view opposing רבי מאיר

steps.whyThisMatters: This line is the key to the refutation: it says plainly that, for רבי מאיר, a note without a guarantee DOES collect from free property.

phrases.english: For רבי מאיר used to say:
a note that includes a property guarantee
phrases.notes: Some versions say בָּהֶם ("in them"); the corrected wording in square brackets says בּוֹ ("in it"). The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: collects from sold property that is tied to the debt.
And one that does not include a property guarantee
collects from free property.
And the חכמים say:
both this kind and that kind
collect from sold property that is tied to the debt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and explains the reasoning behind the rulings in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: How much a note without אחריות נכסים collects according to רבי מאיר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of the same ברייתא

steps.title: Announcing the refutation and restating רבי אלעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares a refutation of רבי אלעזר and first restates his two claims. For רבי מאיר, a note without a guarantee collects nothing at all. Neither side worries about קנוניא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רבי אלעזר in one matter. He said: according to רבי מאיר, a note without a property guarantee collects neither from sold property nor from free property. And he said: both according to רבי מאיר and according to the רבנן, we do not worry about collusion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces that the ברייתא refutes רבי אלעזר. It lays out exactly what he said, setting up the next step, where the ברייתא will be shown to clash with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in Step 2, רבי אלעזר said that when the borrower admits, everyone returns the note. That means nobody fears the two sides are plotting together. He also tied the argument to a note without a guarantee being worth nothing for רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation: a strong disproof from a source
In one (matter)
Collusion: borrower and lender plotting together, for example to use a paid note to take land from buyers
We are concerned (about a possibility)

phrases.english: This is a refutation of רבי אלעזר in one matter,
for he said: according to רבי מאיר,
a note that does not include a property guarantee
does not collect from sold property
and not from free property.

phrases.aramaic: וְקָאָמַר: בֵּין לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר בֵּין לְרַבָּנַן
phrases.english: And he says: both according to רבי מאיר and according to the רבנן,
we are not concerned about collusion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the ברייתא from Steps 5-6 into an attack on רבי אלעזר by first restating his position.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's explanation of the משנה (Step 2)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His two claims (a note without a guarantee collects nothing for רבי מאיר, and nobody fears קנוניא) are about to be shown to contradict the ברייתא.

steps.title: The ברייתא contradicts both of רבי אלעזר's claims
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא shows that a note without a guarantee does collect from free property. Its ruling that a guaranteed note is not returned even when both agree shows that everyone fears קנוניא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches: a note without a property guarantee cannot collect from sold property, but it can collect from free property. And it teaches that both according to רבי מאיר and according to the רבנן, we worry about collusion. For it teaches: even if both agree, he should not return it to either one. Clearly, we worry about collusion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the ברייתא's words against each of רבי אלעזר's claims and shows they clash. This completes the refutation announced in Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First clash: רבי אלעזר said a note without a guarantee collects nothing, but the ברייתא says it collects from free property. Second clash: רבי אלעזר said nobody fears קנוניא, but the ברייתא refuses to return a guaranteed note even when both sides agree. The only reason to refuse is fear that they are plotting together.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches (quoting a ברייתא or משנה)
It certainly collects
Clearly / this shows that

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves two things against רבי אלעזר: (1) for רבי מאיר, a note without אחריות נכסים still collects from free property; (2) everyone fears קנוניא, since a guaranteed note is not returned even when both sides agree. This fits רבי יוחנן's reading.

phrases.english: But the ברייתא teaches:
a note that does not include a property guarantee
is what cannot collect from sold property,
but from free property it certainly collects.

phrases.aramaic: וְקָתָנֵי: בֵּין לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר בֵּין לְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: And it teaches that both according to רבי מאיר and according to the רבנן,
we are concerned about collusion.

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָתָנֵי: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם מוֹדִים
phrases.english: For it teaches: even though both of them agree,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַחְזִיר לֹא לָזֶה וְלֹא לָזֶה.
phrases.english: he should not return it, not to this one and not to that one.
Clearly, we are concerned about collusion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the refutation set up in Step 7 by matching each of רבי אלעזר's claims against the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's two claims restated in Step 7
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says a note without a guarantee collects from free property, and it refuses to return a guaranteed note even when both agree, which shows a fear of קנוניא. Both points contradict רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: Aren't two claims refuted, not one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges its own earlier count. It said the ברייתא refutes only one point of רבי אלעזר, but the refutation seemed to hit two of his points.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a mismatch. It announced that the ברייתא refutes one point of רבי אלעזר, but it then showed two of his claims being disproven, so it asks how the count of 'one' can be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 the גמרא listed two claims of רבי אלעזר. The first was that, for רבי מאיר, a note without a guarantee collects nothing at all. The second was that no one worries about קנוניא. Step 8 knocked down both of these, so the earlier statement that only one point was refuted now looks wrong. The גמרא will need to explain why these count as one.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)
these
two

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new attack on רבי אלעזר's opinion. The גמרא is only questioning its own count of how many of his points were refuted.

phrases.english: But aren't these
phrases.notes: 'These' means the two claims of רבי אלעזר that the ברייתא just disproved in Steps 7–8.

phrases.english: two [points]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the count given in Step 4, using the two-part refutation laid out in Steps 7–8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier statement (Step 4) that the ברייתא refutes only one point of רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The refutation actually disproved two separate claims of רבי אלעזר: that an unguaranteed note collects nothing, and that no one fears קנוניא. So the count of 'one' seems wrong.
